Coordinated, Not Costume:

Inside the Year's Best Celebrity Couple Style Moments

BeyondStyle Editorial5 min read
Timothee Chalamet and Kylie Jenner, head to toe in custom Chrome Hearts, at the Los Angeles premiere of Marty Supreme on December 8, 2025.

Matching outfits used to mean holiday pajamas or a rushed Halloween costume. The current crop of famous couples treats it as its own genre, built from custom leather, borrowed fur, and the kind of color coordination that takes a stylist and a group chat to pull off. None of it reads as a bit. It reads like two people who like the same closet.

Here are five pairings worth studying, from a traffic-cone orange red carpet moment to a black tie debut that quietly told an engagement story of its own.

Zendaya and Tom Holland, In Merlot

On October 24, 2024, Zendaya stepped out in New York for the launch of Tom Holland's non-alcoholic beer brand, Bero, in a custom burgundy leather gown from Louis Vuitton by Nicolas Ghesquiere, styled by her longtime collaborator Law Roach. The plunge-neck dress cinched at the waist with gold hardware and pooled into a floor-sweeping hem. Holland matched her in a burgundy mock-neck top and black trousers, a nod, stylist Crystalle Cox later said, to his favorite Bero flavor.

Zendaya in custom Louis Vuitton, Tom Holland in a matching burgundy top, leaving Bero's New York launch party.

Kylie Jenner and Timothee Chalamet, In Traffic-Cone Orange

Only the couple's second red carpet appearance together, this one came dressed as a marketing stunt. Chalamet had spent weeks promoting Marty Supreme, his A24 ping pong drama, in orange, and he brought Jenner into it for the film's Los Angeles premiere. Both wore custom Chrome Hearts: Jenner in a cutout column gown with a leg slit, Chalamet in a leather suit with a silk shirt and Chrome Hearts take on a Timberland boot, plus a black ping-pong paddle case slung across his chest.

Neither piece is for sale. Chrome Hearts built both looks specifically for the premiere, which is increasingly the norm for a couple's red carpet debut moment: custom over off-the-rack, so no one else can show up in the same dress.

Hailey and Justin Bieber, In Matching Leather

The Biebers are typically cited as the "overdressed girlfriend, underdressed boyfriend" archetype, but a May 2023 dinner in London broke the pattern. Hailey wore a black zip-up leather jacket with straight-leg light wash jeans and an emerald green shoulder bag, while Justin matched her in an oversized black leather trucker jacket, distressed baggy jeans, and a red baseball cap. Same fabric, same palette, opposite silhouettes.

Justin and Hailey Bieber in coordinating black leather, out for dinner in London.

Rihanna and A$AP Rocky, In Fur

A few days after A$AP Rocky accepted the CFDA Fashion Icon Award, the couple stepped out in Paris in matching brown fur, Rihanna in a cropped jacket over baggy jeans and a white tee, Rocky in a floor-length duster coat. Rocky finished the look with pieces from his own creative agency, AWGE: a fur tote bearing the label's logo, and a Chanel trapper hat.

Rihanna and A$AP Rocky in coordinating fur, photographed on a Paris street in November 2025. Rocky's tote is from his label, AWGE.
Price Check
$1,925 · Chanel fur trapper hat

The one piece in this outfit anyone can actually buy. Everything else, the coats, the AWGE tote, is either custom or not on the market.

Hailee Steinfeld and Josh Allen, In Black Tie

Steinfeld and the Buffalo Bills quarterback made their first public appearance as an engaged couple at the 2025 NFL Honors in New Orleans, both dressed head to toe in black. Steinfeld wore a strapless velvet gown with a diamond choker, Allen a classic black suit with a tie to match. It was a low-key palette for a milestone night, and it let the engagement ring do most of the talking.

Hailee Steinfeld and Josh Allen at the 2025 NFL Honors, their first red carpet appearance as an engaged couple.

The common thread across all five isn't the color story or the budget. It's restraint. Every pairing here picked one idea, a hue, a fabric, a formality level, and let both people run with it separately instead of forcing identical outfits. That's the actual trick to dressing as a unit without looking like you're wearing a costume.
